column4: The village of Brienz/Binzauls in the Swiss Alps [46.6688, 9.5953] was evacuated between 9 and 12 May 2023...The village of Brienz/Brinzauls is situated on an old deep-seated mountain slope deformation extending from Piz Linard (2,767 m asl) to the Albula river (900 m asl)...Since summer 2022 the most rapid compartment [referred to as the Insel"] was identified in a steep convergent slope directly above the village of Brienz, extending between an elevation of of 1,400 masl and 1,700 masl...In June accelerations further increased leading to velocities of up to 80 m/day before the compartment collapsed on 15 June 2023...Only about 80% of the “Insel” compartment collapsed and the remaining sector in the east moves today with velocities of up to 100 mm/day" - Quote from Loew and others (2023)
Volume_low estimate taken from a preliminary analysis by Loew and others (2023). This estimate is also consistent with the volume provided in Häusler and others (2025) (Refid 376).
Before and after imagery of the event can be see at https://www.planet.com/stories/brienzlandslide-aE99YfuVR (Shugar, 2023).

Volume estimate of 2 million m3 taken from Loew and others (2025) and represents the Insel compartment of the active Brienz complex. This value was estimated before the event occurred, using vector analyses (Loew and others, 2025).

Systematic GPS monitoring of the area around the future Insel compartment started already in the year 2009, and was continuously upgraded with the installation of a Total Station and many reflectors in 2011, a Doppler radar for permanent rockfall monitoring in 2018, a ground-based interferometric radar in 2019, and several time-lapse cameras, some with automated digital image correlation processing (since 2022) - Quote from Loew and others (2025)

The currently active landslide mass with moving rates larger than 0.5 m/year has a total volume of about 170 million m3, covers an area of 2.5 km2, reactivates pre-existing sliding zones in the lower reaches (between Brienz and the Albula river), and develops new rupture, sliding, and toppling surfaces in the upper reaches - Quote from Loew and others (2025)

The collapse started with multiple secondary failures at the toe creating dry granular flows mainly composed of Allgäu schists. The main seismic shock recorded by the Swiss Seismological Survey also occurred at 23:38 - Quote from Loew and others (2025)

Häusler and others (2025) provide an investigation of the Brienz-Brinzaul landslide complex using ambient vibration data, from seismic station BRIZ2, to provide insight on the local behavior of slope instability. They note decreases in resonance frequency after December 2020 and November 2022 and interpret these decreases as "a reduction in material stiffness attributed to the disintegration of landslide material" (Häusler and others, 2025).
Manconi and others (2024) provide an analysis of SAR data at the Brienz-Brinzauls landslide complex to explore surface displacements between 1992-2020, before the 2023-06-15 event.

Raw waveforms from closest stations. Data was demeaned but no other processing was applied. Dashed lines show approximate start and end times of event (from database). Figure generation is automated and there may be artifacts present.

High frequency (1-5 Hz) ground velocity waveforms from closest stations with detections. Dashed lines show approximate start and end times of event (from database). Waveforms are corrected for station response after removing the mean. Figure generation is automated and there may be artifacts present. Clipped waveforms have not been removed before station correction so check raw plots before interpreting high amplitude signals.
Spectrograms of velocity waveforms corrected for station sensitivity from closest stations with detections. Figure generation is automated and there may be artifacts present

Multitaper spectra (same units as Power Spectral Density) of velocity waveforms corrected for station sensitivity from closest stations with detections. Linear trend was removed and a taper was applied before generating spectra. Figure generation is automated and there may be artifacts present. Since station response was not removed to avoid adding artifacts at low frequencies for short and intermediate period stations, the lower frequency amplitudes should be interpreted with care.
